# Team Workflow

## a) Repository and Report Structure

Jennifer created the shared public GitHub repository and prepared the initial structure of the project on the `main` branch before the group started working. This included the master Quarto document, the section files, and the general organization of the notebook.

To allow all three team members to work at the same time while reducing the risk of merge conflicts, the report was divided into **11 separate Quarto sub-documents**. Each sub-document corresponds to one of the main headings or sections of the assignment that had to be completed. This made it easy to keep track of the work and clearly identify which part of the assignment was being developed.

Before the analysis started, headings and subheadings were also created inside each section document. This gave each team member a clear structure to follow and made it clear what information, code, results, and conclusions had to be included in each section. It also ensured that all sub-documents would fit together consistently when included in the master Quarto document.

A master Quarto document includes all 11 sub-documents when the final report is rendered, allowing the sections to be developed separately but combined into one organized final report. A table of contents was also created in the master document so that the different sections and subsections could be found easily.

We also used **11 Git branches**, with one branch corresponding to each section document. The branch name matched the section file, making it easy to identify the purpose of each branch and follow the progress of the assignment.
